summary.oneLiner: Bank of India's best-quality quarter in the current cycle: net profit **INR 3,068 cr (+36.23% YoY)** on operating profit **INR 5,051 cr (+25.99%)**, with asset quality at a cycle-best (**GNPA 1.81%**, −111 bps YoY; **NNPA 0.51%**; **PCR 93.83%**; slippage ratio **0.24%**; credit cost **0.15%**) and SMA ≥INR 5 cr down to **INR 4,090 cr / 0.52% of the standard book**. Growth is broad — global business **+16.57%** to INR 17.55 lakh cr, global gross advances **+18.64%**, RAM **+19.75%** — but the operating leverage is *liability-side fragile*: **NIM 2.52% is below the year-ago 2.55%**, CASA ratio has slipped to **36.68%** with management conceding a ~3% fall in both CASA and retail-TD share, and the profit beat leans on treasury/other income (**+19.07%**) and a **~46% cost-to-income that management itself guides back up to 48–49%**. The swing factor for the next two quarters is the RBI's foreign-currency window: a self-set **USD 1.2 bn FCNR(B) target by 30-Sep-2026** against only **>USD 200 mn garnered**, plus USD 2 bn OFCB/MTN and ~USD 1 bn ECB to make ~**USD 4.2 bn by 31-Dec-2026**.

6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **The overseas franchise is the genuine differentiator, and it is now being repriced rather than just grown.**
  "Bank of India was the foremost Bank with global operations" (analyst) — presence in **more than 15 countries**,
  international business first time above INR 2.5 lakh cr (closed ~INR 2.56 lakh cr). The moat evidence is that
  management can *choose* to swap 32% low-margin trade finance for higher-yield corporate paper rather than defend
  volume — a pricing-power option most PSU peers lack.
- **NRI deposit franchise as a funding moat: "more than 3 lakh NRI, PIO and OIC customers"** across ~250 AD/NRI
  branches and 13 FGMOs, which is why a USD 1.2 bn FCNR target is self-set rather than market-taken.
- **Gold-loan underwriting quality as an operating moat** — an INR 57,000 cr book growing 52% YoY with
  **"NPA is less than Rs. 100 crores"** and a 3-notice/90-day realisation SOP; scale plus near-zero credit loss at
  a 9.10% yield.
- **Collection machinery** — "our zonal collections are doing excellent work which is enabling us to reduce our SMA
  numbers overall", evidenced by SMA ≥INR 5 cr falling >INR 7,000 cr → ~INR 4,700 cr → INR 4,090 cr over four quarters.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **NIM 2.52% vs 2.55% YoY**, guided to 2.55–2.60% for FY27 — an *expansion* guide off a *contracted* base.
- **Rate-cycle mechanics disclosed: "60% of our book is through the repo external benchmark"** — so a repo hike
  helps NII and hurts the investment book, and vice versa ("many things are not in our control in that manner").
  This is precisely why Q1's treasury-led other income is not extrapolable.
- **Cost of deposits is falling** (analyst cited −15 bps) **despite CASA and retail-TD share each falling ~3%** —
  management's explanation is deliberate mix engineering: "there is lot of traction in fixed deposits up to 25
  crores… we have garnered lot of deposit between the **3 crore and the 25 crore bucket**. There we see the rate of
  interest is much finer than taking a bulk deposit of say 500 crore or a 1000 crore or a 750 crores."
- **But CASA dilution is admitted as growth-funding:** "our credit growth is very robust… So, we have to raise
  resources… we have been taking bulk deposits. Deposits which are above 3 crores also. So, in order to do that,
  obviously this percentage of CASA percentage and the retail term deposit percentage has come down."
- **Yield-on-advances levers:** more MCLR-linked lending; mid-corporate (19 branches, INR 25–250 cr); swap out
  low-margin international trade finance; grow gold loans at ~9.10%.
- **Cost-to-income ~46% in Q1, guided 48–49% FY27.** Cost actions: **~300 ATMs removed** — "in some of the Capex
  models, where we've thought that these ATMs were running into losses, much hits were not there. So, there we have
  clearly moved out of those ATMs. That is part of our cost optimization strategy also which has helped us to also
  reduce our cost to income ratio."
- **FCNR economics** (see §6) are the explicit cost-of-deposit lever into H2: "the FCNR deposits that will be coming
  will helping us in reducing the cost of deposit."
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- No large physical capex flagged; expansion is **channel + technology**, and one line is explicitly *negative* capex

- **Technology spend is the capex story:** "we are spending much money as far as IT, digital and cybersecurity is
  concerned… our loan operating system is also well established"; Data Lake → CRM Next lead flow; AI capabilities.
  Management frames FY27 as the harvest year: **"now the time has come for us after spending so much of money that

- **Network/vertical build:** Centralized Sales Vertical; SVB Mumbai; Centralized Video-CIP centre; 19 emerging
  corporate credit branches; ~250 FCNR/NRI-enabled AD branches across 13 FGMOs.
- **Watch-items with dates:** FCNR(B) window **30-Sep-2026**; OFCB/MTN window **31-Dec-2026**; ECLGS scheme end

capital allocation:
- **CRAR 18.69% (from 17.39% YoY)** — comfortably self-funded; **no equity raise was discussed or sought** on the call.
- Capital is being deployed into **advances growth (+18.64% global)** rather than returned; the balance-sheet
  strategy is explicitly to grow "in a very secular manner… RAM advances in retail, agriculture, MSME… Mid Corporate
  book… Corporate book… International book… co-lending, pool purchase, supply chain financing and also our TREDs
  book" so that "any impact which is there in any particular geography, sector or segment we are able to obviate."
- **External capital/funding raise is debt-side, not equity-side:** ~USD 4.2 bn (FCNR-B + OFCB + MTN + ECB) by
  31-Dec-2026.
- **Subsidiary monetisation deferred:** BOI Mutual Fund (AUM ~INR 16,000–17,000 cr) — "we need to grow the AUM
  further before we hit the market. So at this moment there are no plans. But at the right time definitely we may plan."
- **No AS-15 provision reversal taken** (peers did) — a conservative capital/earnings choice.
risks & watch-items:
- **NIM is the weak link.** 2.52% is *below* the 2.55% year-ago print, yet FY27 guidance is 2.55–2.60%; management
  concedes "NIMs are under challenge with the present interest rate scenario." With **60% of the book on the repo
  external benchmark**, spread direction is largely exogenous.
- **Liability-mix erosion.** CASA ratio 36.68% with a ~3% YoY fall, and retail term deposits also −3%, replaced by
  INR 3–25 cr bulk-ish deposits. Management attributes it to a **structural shift of household savings** into
  "equity, in mutual fund, in insurance products and also in other wealth management products like gold and… real
  estate." This is a permanent headwind, not a quarter effect.
- **Earnings-quality dependence on treasury.** The Q1 beat leans on other income (+19.07%) that the questioner
  attributed to revaluation gains, plus a ~46% CIR management itself guides back to 48–49%.
- **West Asia crisis / supply-chain stress in named sectors:** "There are certain sectors where we feel that there
  has been direct impact, particularly sectors like **chemical**, sectors like **ceramics** and also sectors where
  import and exports are there, particularly **import of oil or gas**… because of the supply chain crisis which is
  happening in the West Asia there is also **increase in the working capital cycle**."
- **MSME stress is being masked by ECLGS.** The INR 6,000 cr sanctioned / INR 4,600 cr disbursed (→INR 8,000 cr)
  scheme is explicitly a bridge: "The MSME accounts where there is certain stress because of the increase in their
  working capital cycle due to the West Asia crisis. They have already availed or will be availing the ECLGS scheme."
  Watch what slippage does when the scheme ends.
- **Monsoon risk flagged for agri/retail:** "with this present crisis which is going on of West Asia and also the
  thing which is there, the problem with the monsoon, we feel that it is better to be very watchful"; the opening
  remarks also cited "the uneven progress of the monsoon and its implications for food prices."
- **Unsecured retail already showing industry stress** — low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans deliberately
  throttled to +3%.
- **FCNR execution gap:** >USD 200 mn garnered against a USD 1.2 bn target due 30-Sep-2026, i.e. ~83% still to raise
  in ~2 months; and the leverage economics are admitted to be deteriorating — analyst: "the dollar demand is tight.
  So, the spread is reduced compared to what was initially offered", MD: **"Exactly."** On the leveraged-portion
  spread: "at this juncture will not be able to tell in detail… it's a moving target."
- **International book growth will look weak by design** — trade-finance swap-out means "you may not see a very high
  delta" in international advances.
- **PSU-bank consolidation is an unpriced binary** — management explicitly refuses to comment; an analyst raised
  "informal consultations have started on PSU banks mergers."
- **Perception gap acknowledged, not addressed with an action** — asked whether investors recognise the
  transformation, the reply was "it is for the investment community to decide basis the numbers and to take a call."
management quality / tone:
- **Numerate, specific, and unusually willing to give hard dates and hard targets** (USD 1.2 bn/30-Sep, USD 4.2 bn/
  31-Dec, INR 8,000 cr ECLGS, 3 lakh credit cards, gold book INR 57,000 cr at 9.10% yield with <INR 100 cr NPA).
  Karnatak answered in reverse order through multi-part questions without dropping items.
- **Candour is genuine on the uncomfortable questions.** He conceded the CASA/retail-TD decline outright ("yes, you
  are right"), agreed with the analyst that FCNR leverage spreads have compressed ("Exactly"), refused to quote a
  leverage spread he could not stand behind, declined the AS-15 reversal that peers took, and declined to give a
  forward PSL number ("presently at this juncture will not be able to give").
- **Deliberately conservative on unsecured retail** — accepting 3% personal-loan growth to protect asset quality is a
  choice, not an outcome, and he said so.
- **Guidance discipline:** FY27 advances/deposits guidance "stays unchanged" despite a Q1 that ran ahead of it, and
  he pushed CIR guidance *up* from the Q1 print rather than anchoring to the flattering number — the opposite of
  guidance-flattering behaviour. An analyst noted "the guidance and the actual performance is a big mismatch."
- **Weak spots:** no repeatability comment on treasury income; the investor-perception question drew a
  non-answer; and management would not engage at all on merger speculation (defensible, but leaves a live overhang).
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The +36% PAT and the 2.52% NIM tell opposite stories.** Spreads contracted YoY; the earnings beat is credit-cost
  normalisation (0.15% vs 0.17%), non-interest income (+19.07%, treasury-aided) and a ~46% CIR that management is
  guiding *away from*. Underwrite the credit-cost improvement, discount the rest.
- **BOI is deliberately trading CASA share for growth funding.** Most PSU banks defend the CASA optic; BOI openly
  swapped it for INR 3–25 cr deposits to fund 18.6% advance growth — and still got cost of deposits down. That is a
  liability-management call, not a franchise failure, but it structurally caps NIM upside.
- **Financialization of household savings is now stated by a PSU bank as its own deposit headwind** — "there has
  been a structural change as far as the saving pattern is concerned in India… investing also in equity, in mutual
  fund, in insurance products and also… gold and… real estate." The CASA-erosion trade and the AMC/broking
  bull-case are the same trade seen from opposite sides of the balance sheet.
- **The FCNR window is being used as a NIM instrument, not a deposit-mobilisation exercise** — CRR/SLR-exempt,
  RBI-hedged, ~50 bps clean spread vs ~7% bulk deposits. The USD 1.2 bn is small versus a INR 9.58 lakh cr deposit
  base, but it lands entirely on the marginal cost of funds, which is what the 2.55–2.60% NIM guide depends on.
- **The gold-loan book is the quietest big number on the call** — INR 57,000 cr growing 52% YoY at 9.10% yield with
  <INR 100 cr NPA. It was not in the opening remarks and only surfaced because an analyst noticed it was missing
  from slide 7 ("somehow gold loans is not mentioned here").
- **The international strategy has inverted:** BOI is now *shrinking* its highest-volume international product (32%
  trade finance) to lift margin — expect flattering NIM and unflattering international growth in the same prints.
- **ECLGS uptake is a leading stress indicator, not a positive.** INR 6,000 cr sanctioned rising to a projected
  INR 8,000 cr means MSME working-capital cycles are stretching; the SMA book looks clean *partly because* the
  scheme is absorbing it.
- **No AS-15 reversal while peers took one** means BOI's Q1 PAT is cleaner than a like-for-like peer comparison
  suggests — a rare case where the conservative bank prints the bigger growth number anyway.

  normalisation (0.15% vs 0.17%), non-interest income (+19.07%, treasury-aided) and a ~46% CIR that management is
  guiding *away from*. Underwrite the credit-cost improvement, discount the rest.
- **BOI is deliberately trading CASA share for growth funding.** Most PSU banks defend the CASA optic; BOI openly
  swapped it for INR 3–25 cr deposits to fund 18.6% advance growth — and still got cost of deposits down. That is a
  liability-management call, not a franchise failure, but it structurally caps NIM upside.
- **Financialization of household savings is now stated by a PSU bank as its own deposit headwind** — "there has
  been a structural change as far as the saving pattern is concerned in India… investing also in equity, in mutual
  fund, in insurance products and also… gold and… real estate." The CASA-erosion trade and the AMC/broking
  bull-case are the same trade seen from opposite sides of the balance sheet.
- **The FCNR window is being used as a NIM instrument, not a deposit-mobilisation exercise** — CRR/SLR-exempt,

- **ECLGS uptake is a leading stress indicator, not a positive.** INR 6,000 cr sanctioned rising to a projected

hero.oneLiner: Bank of India's best-quality quarter in the current cycle: net profit **INR 3,068 cr (+36.23% YoY)** on operating profit **INR 5,051 cr (+25.99%)**, with asset quality at a cycle-best (**GNPA 1.81%**, −111 bps YoY; **NNPA 0.51%**; **PCR 93.83%**; slippage ratio **0.24%**; credit cost **0.15%**) and SMA ≥INR 5 cr down to **INR 4,090 cr / 0.52% of the standard book**. Growth is broad — global business **+16.57%** to INR 17.55 lakh cr, global gross advances **+18.64%**, RAM **+19.75%** — but the operating leverage is *liability-side fragile*: **NIM 2.52% is below the year-ago 2.55%**, CASA ratio has slipped to **36.68%** with management conceding a ~3% fall in both CASA and retail-TD share, and the profit beat leans on treasury/other income (**+19.07%**) and a **~46% cost-to-income that management itself guides back up to 48–49%**. The swing factor for the next two quarters is the RBI's foreign-currency window: a self-set **USD 1.2 bn FCNR(B) target by 30-Sep-2026** against only **>USD 200 mn garnered**, plus USD 2 bn OFCB/MTN and ~USD 1 bn ECB to make ~**USD 4.2 bn by 31-Dec-2026**.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Scale headline: "Global Business crosses ₹17.50 Lakh Crore with 16.57% YoY Growth" — Global Business Mix ₹17,55,699 Cr at 30.06.26, made up of Global Deposits ₹9,57,924 Cr (+14.90% YoY) and Global Advances ₹7,97,775 Cr (+18.64% YoY).
- Stated strategic tilt to granular lending: "The Bank continues to strengthen its focus on the RAM portfolio, with its contribution to Gross Domestic Advances increasing year-on-year" — RAM ₹3,28,048 Cr (30.06.25) → ₹3,83,278 Cr (31.03.26) → ₹3,92,833 Cr (30.06.26), with RAM Advances at 58.03% / 58.57% / 58.30% of Gross Domestic Advances across the three dates.
- Government ownership is presented as a credit anchor: "The bank continues to maintain strong domestic credit ratings of AAA / AA+ across leading rating agencies, supported by a majority Government shareholding of 73.38%".
- An international franchise most domestic peers lack: 46 total foreign offices — 20 overseas branches, 4 overseas subsidiaries (23 offices), 1 overseas associate, 1 representative office and 1 IFSC Banking Unit (IBU) at GIFT City — "Spread across 5 continents and 14 countries"; overseas business mix ₹2,56,903 Cr at 30.06.26.
- Priority-sector positioning: "Priority Sector lending across categories exceed the regulatory targets as on 30.06.2026" — Priority Sector at 47.11% of ANBC vs a 40.00% target, Agriculture 19.85% vs 18.00%, Small and Marginal Farmers 14.22% vs 10.00%, Weaker Section 17.95% vs 12.00%, Micro Enterprises 9.58% vs 7.50%.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **RAM (58.30% of advances, +19.75%)** is the declared growth engine; within it **gold loan** is called out as
  "one of our clear strategies as far as the growth in the RAM Advances are concerned."
- **Gold loans — book ~INR 57,000 cr as on 30-Jun-2026, growing ~52% YoY, yield "more than 9% somewhere around
  9.10%", NPA "less than Rs. 100 crores."** Recovery SOP: "after giving three notices within 90 days, we sell the
  gold and realize the money."
- **Personal loans grew only ~3%** — deliberate: "we have put certain guardrails… we felt that the **low ticket
  personal loans are at risk**… the **non-salaried personal loans were also creating some issues**." Focus shifted
  to salaried/service-sector borrowers with salary credit into BOI accounts and NACH mandates.
- **International book ~INR 2.56 lakh cr (first time >INR 2.5 lakh cr)** — but deliberately low-delta from here:
  "around **32% of our international loan book is trade finance where the margins are very less**. We are trying to
  now replace this trade finance book with the Indian corporates and domestic corporates." 15+ countries.
- **GIFT City** — "Gift City is our key strategy as far as lending is concerned and there is very good book is
  getting created."
- **BOI Mutual Fund** — AUM ~INR 16,000–17,000 cr; monetisation deferred until AUM scales.
- **BOI Services Ltd** — "facilitating a proposed mechanism to deploy dedicated field staff on the ground" to
  revamp Cash Management Services.
- **Bank of India Kenya** — mobile-banking app live with "seamless **M-PESA** integration."
- **Credit cards** — RuPay Select, RuPay Platinum, Visa Gold International; "we have revamped our credit card
  offering entirely last quarter… now we intend to increase it" → 3 lakh cards by FY27-end.
- **New Strategic Business Branch (SVB), Mumbai** — "dedicated to capturing high value pool buyouts, co-lending,
  TReDS business and also supply chain financing."
- **Centralized Sales Vertical** — "end to end responsibility for driving customer acquisition, enhancing business
  productivity, and boosting revenue."

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- **Total loan pipeline "more than 1 lakh crores"** — "a very secular loan book."
- **Corporate + international pipeline ~INR 70,000 cr** — "our corporate pipeline is somewhere around 70,000 crore,
  as we speak which includes our pipeline for domestic corporates and also for the international corporates put
  together and some of it in the international side is coming from the Gift City itself."
- **Remaining ~INR 30,000 cr** of the pipeline sits in "RAM Advances digital book and also the pool purchase, pool
  lending, TREDs and supply chain financing."
- **International pipeline centres:** GIFT City plus New York, London, Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore — "this pipeline
  is coming not only from Indian corporates but also local corporates over there."
- **ECLGS pipeline:** INR 6,000 cr sanctioned → INR 4,600 cr disbursed → ~INR 8,000 cr expected by scheme end.
- **Data-Lake/CRM-Next analytics-sourced business: "we have built a business of more than 18,000 crores."**

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 guidance reiterated, unchanged:** "our guidance for FY27 stays unchanged – global advances to grow by
  **15-16%**, and global deposits by **13-14%**."
- **ROA:** "we would want to have a **1% and above ROA in FY27** on a consistent basis QoQ basis."
- **Global NIM:** "our guidance for the global NIM is somewhere around **2.55% to 2.60% for FY27**" — explicitly
  caveated: "NIMs are under challenge with the present interest rate scenario… and also the situation… because of
  the West Asia crisis."
- **Cost-to-income:** "during FY27 we should be somewhere around **48% - 49%** on a consistent basis" (vs ~46% in Q1).
- **FCNR(B): "our target is, to achieve the number of 1.2 billion by the 30th of September."** Currently
  "we have already garnered **more than 200 million** of FCNRB deposit." RBI window closes 30-Sep-2026.
- **OFCB / MTN: "we have also set ourselves a target that will be raising around USD 2 billion"** — window
  "up to 31st December 2026."
- **ECB:** "in four to five accounts we have already given in principle approvals of around **500 million** and we
  are very confident that there also we will be doing around **1 billion**."
- **Combined external funding:** "put together, we will be somewhere around **4.2 billion by the end of the 31st of
  December** with FCNR, OFCB, MTN and the ECB."
- **ECLGS:** "we have already sanctioned somewhere around **6,000 crores**… out of which **4,600 crores** has already
  been disbursed and we expect that by the time the scheme comes to an end… around **8,000 crore** of sanctions and
  disbursal."
- **Credit cards:** "The target which we have set is to have a **credit card base of 3 lakh by end of the FY27**."
- **Slippage trajectory:** "Normally, the Q1 slippages in Bank of India are higher than the other quarters and with
  the progress of time the fresh slippages will go down further in the coming quarters."
- **Yield on advances:** "there will be a **pause in reduction** and from there we'll be able to grow that yield on
  advances" — levers: more MCLR-linked advances; mid-corporate via 19 emerging-corporate-credit branches
  (INR 25 cr–250 cr ticket).
- **PSL income:** "we will definitely have an opportunity of doing some PSL in the ensuing quarters of Q2 and Q3
  also… presently at this juncture will not be able to give but definitely we will have some legroom."
- **BOI Mutual Fund IPO:** "It is yet a bit far off to go to the market… at this moment there are **no plans**."
- **PSU-bank merger:** "we have **no comments**, there has been **no discussion with us**. So, it is only for the
  Government to answer this question or the RBI."

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **FCNR(B) + OFCB/MTN + ECB stack (~USD 4.2 bn by 31-Dec-2026)** — CRR/SLR-exempt funding with RBI bearing the
  hedging cost: "if you even see the gap which is there for the 5 year FCNR at 6.5% with the hedging cost being
  taken care by the RBI. So we are getting a **clean spread of around 50 basis point**… and there is **no CRR/ SLR
  also to be maintained** on those deposits." Rates offered: **6.25% (3 yr), 6.30% (3–4 yr), 6.50% (5 yr)** vs bulk
  deposits "at somewhere around 7%".
- **FCNR leverage product — up to 9x, board-approved:** "the approval from the Board on the leverage, we have taken
  at **nine times**, we have a matrix for that maximum, we will go up to nine times… already certain discussions are
  there with some of the large HNI customers who are seeking leverage from us." Currently "majority of which is in
  the core FCNR deposit and leverage much is not there."
- **NRI franchise as the FCNR moat:** "more than **3 lakh NRI, PIO and OIC customers**"; ~250 AD/NRI-enabled
  branches across 13 FGMOs.
- **Mid-corporate up-yield play** — 19 emerging-corporate-credit branches, INR 25–250 cr tickets, where "the rate of
  interests are better. The LC/BG commissions are better which gives us non interest income and the process fees are
  also better."
- **Digital lending at scale — "At least 22% of our entire domestic book in the domestic credit is now digital
  sanctions"**, plus analytics-sourced leads (Data Lake → CRM Next → branches) = >INR 18,000 cr business built.
- **Fee/float engines:** cash-management revamp via BOI Services; TReDS, co-lending, pool buyouts and supply-chain
  finance consolidated into the new SVB Mumbai.
- **Digital retail products launched:** Virtual Personalized RuPay Debit Card (self-activated in BOI Omni Neo app);
  BOI Star Choice Current Account (customer picks the last 7 digits of the account number); Centralized Video-CIP
  centre in Mumbai for end-to-end digital account opening.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **NIM 2.52% vs 2.55% YoY**, guided to 2.55–2.60% for FY27 — an *expansion* guide off a *contracted* base.
- **Rate-cycle mechanics disclosed: "60% of our book is through the repo external benchmark"** — so a repo hike
  helps NII and hurts the investment book, and vice versa ("many things are not in our control in that manner").
  This is precisely why Q1's treasury-led other income is not extrapolable.
- **Cost of deposits is falling** (analyst cited −15 bps) **despite CASA and retail-TD share each falling ~3%** —
  management's explanation is deliberate mix engineering: "there is lot of traction in fixed deposits up to 25
  crores… we have garnered lot of deposit between the **3 crore and the 25 crore bucket**. There we see the rate of
  interest is much finer than taking a bulk deposit of say 500 crore or a 1000 crore or a 750 crores."
- **But CASA dilution is admitted as growth-funding:** "our credit growth is very robust… So, we have to raise
  resources… we have been taking bulk deposits. Deposits which are above 3 crores also. So, in order to do that,
  obviously this percentage of CASA percentage and the retail term deposit percentage has come down."
- **Yield-on-advances levers:** more MCLR-linked lending; mid-corporate (19 branches, INR 25–250 cr); swap out
  low-margin international trade finance; grow gold loans at ~9.10%.
- **Cost-to-income ~46% in Q1, guided 48–49% FY27.** Cost actions: **~300 ATMs removed** — "in some of the Capex
  models, where we've thought that these ATMs were running into losses, much hits were not there. So, there we have
  clearly moved out of those ATMs. That is part of our cost optimization strategy also which has helped us to also
  reduce our cost to income ratio."
- **FCNR economics** (see §6) are the explicit cost-of-deposit lever into H2: "the FCNR deposits that will be coming
  will helping us in reducing the cost of deposit."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **CRAR 18.69% (from 17.39% YoY)** — comfortably self-funded; **no equity raise was discussed or sought** on the call.
- Capital is being deployed into **advances growth (+18.64% global)** rather than returned; the balance-sheet
  strategy is explicitly to grow "in a very secular manner… RAM advances in retail, agriculture, MSME… Mid Corporate
  book… Corporate book… International book… co-lending, pool purchase, supply chain financing and also our TREDs
  book" so that "any impact which is there in any particular geography, sector or segment we are able to obviate."
- **External capital/funding raise is debt-side, not equity-side:** ~USD 4.2 bn (FCNR-B + OFCB + MTN + ECB) by
  31-Dec-2026.
- **Subsidiary monetisation deferred:** BOI Mutual Fund (AUM ~INR 16,000–17,000 cr) — "we need to grow the AUM
  further before we hit the market. So at this moment there are no plans. But at the right time definitely we may plan."
- **No AS-15 provision reversal taken** (peers did) — a conservative capital/earnings choice.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
- **Numerate, specific, and unusually willing to give hard dates and hard targets** (USD 1.2 bn/30-Sep, USD 4.2 bn/
  31-Dec, INR 8,000 cr ECLGS, 3 lakh credit cards, gold book INR 57,000 cr at 9.10% yield with <INR 100 cr NPA).
  Karnatak answered in reverse order through multi-part questions without dropping items.
- **Candour is genuine on the uncomfortable questions.** He conceded the CASA/retail-TD decline outright ("yes, you
  are right"), agreed with the analyst that FCNR leverage spreads have compressed ("Exactly"), refused to quote a
  leverage spread he could not stand behind, declined the AS-15 reversal that peers took, and declined to give a
  forward PSL number ("presently at this juncture will not be able to give").
- **Deliberately conservative on unsecured retail** — accepting 3% personal-loan growth to protect asset quality is a
  choice, not an outcome, and he said so.
- **Guidance discipline:** FY27 advances/deposits guidance "stays unchanged" despite a Q1 that ran ahead of it, and
  he pushed CIR guidance *up* from the Q1 print rather than anchoring to the flattering number — the opposite of
  guidance-flattering behaviour. An analyst noted "the guidance and the actual performance is a big mismatch."
- **Weak spots:** no repeatability comment on treasury income; the investor-perception question drew a
  non-answer; and management would not engage at all on merger speculation (defensible, but leaves a live overhang).

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)
moat.body:
- **The overseas franchise is the genuine differentiator, and it is now being repriced rather than just grown.**
  "Bank of India was the foremost Bank with global operations" (analyst) — presence in **more than 15 countries**,
  international business first time above INR 2.5 lakh cr (closed ~INR 2.56 lakh cr). The moat evidence is that
  management can *choose* to swap 32% low-margin trade finance for higher-yield corporate paper rather than defend
  volume — a pricing-power option most PSU peers lack.
- **NRI deposit franchise as a funding moat: "more than 3 lakh NRI, PIO and OIC customers"** across ~250 AD/NRI
  branches and 13 FGMOs, which is why a USD 1.2 bn FCNR target is self-set rather than market-taken.
- **Gold-loan underwriting quality as an operating moat** — an INR 57,000 cr book growing 52% YoY with
  **"NPA is less than Rs. 100 crores"** and a 3-notice/90-day realisation SOP; scale plus near-zero credit loss at
  a 9.10% yield.
- **Collection machinery** — "our zonal collections are doing excellent work which is enabling us to reduce our SMA
  numbers overall", evidenced by SMA ≥INR 5 cr falling >INR 7,000 cr → ~INR 4,700 cr → INR 4,090 cr over four quarters.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **NIM is the weak link.** 2.52% is *below* the 2.55% year-ago print, yet FY27 guidance is 2.55–2.60%; management
  concedes "NIMs are under challenge with the present interest rate scenario." With **60% of the book on the repo
  external benchmark**, spread direction is largely exogenous.
- **Liability-mix erosion.** CASA ratio 36.68% with a ~3% YoY fall, and retail term deposits also −3%, replaced by
  INR 3–25 cr bulk-ish deposits. Management attributes it to a **structural shift of household savings** into
  "equity, in mutual fund, in insurance products and also in other wealth management products like gold and… real
  estate." This is a permanent headwind, not a quarter effect.
- **Earnings-quality dependence on treasury.** The Q1 beat leans on other income (+19.07%) that the questioner
  attributed to revaluation gains, plus a ~46% CIR management itself guides back to 48–49%.
- **West Asia crisis / supply-chain stress in named sectors:** "There are certain sectors where we feel that there
  has been direct impact, particularly sectors like **chemical**, sectors like **ceramics** and also sectors where
  import and exports are there, particularly **import of oil or gas**… because of the supply chain crisis which is
  happening in the West Asia there is also **increase in the working capital cycle**."
- **MSME stress is being masked by ECLGS.** The INR 6,000 cr sanctioned / INR 4,600 cr disbursed (→INR 8,000 cr)
  scheme is explicitly a bridge: "The MSME accounts where there is certain stress because of the increase in their
  working capital cycle due to the West Asia crisis. They have already availed or will be availing the ECLGS scheme."
  Watch what slippage does when the scheme ends.
- **Monsoon risk flagged for agri/retail:** "with this present crisis which is going on of West Asia and also the
  thing which is there, the problem with the monsoon, we feel that it is better to be very watchful"; the opening
  remarks also cited "the uneven progress of the monsoon and its implications for food prices."
- **Unsecured retail already showing industry stress** — low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans deliberately
  throttled to +3%.
- **FCNR execution gap:** >USD 200 mn garnered against a USD 1.2 bn target due 30-Sep-2026, i.e. ~83% still to raise
  in ~2 months; and the leverage economics are admitted to be deteriorating — analyst: "the dollar demand is tight.
  So, the spread is reduced compared to what was initially offered", MD: **"Exactly."** On the leveraged-portion
  spread: "at this juncture will not be able to tell in detail… it's a moving target."
- **International book growth will look weak by design** — trade-finance swap-out means "you may not see a very high
  delta" in international advances.
- **PSU-bank consolidation is an unpriced binary** — management explicitly refuses to comment; an analyst raised
  "informal consultations have started on PSU banks mergers."
- **Perception gap acknowledged, not addressed with an action** — asked whether investors recognise the
  transformation, the reply was "it is for the investment community to decide basis the numbers and to take a call."

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The +36% PAT and the 2.52% NIM tell opposite stories.** Spreads contracted YoY; the earnings beat is credit-cost
  normalisation (0.15% vs 0.17%), non-interest income (+19.07%, treasury-aided) and a ~46% CIR that management is
  guiding *away from*. Underwrite the credit-cost improvement, discount the rest.
- **BOI is deliberately trading CASA share for growth funding.** Most PSU banks defend the CASA optic; BOI openly
  swapped it for INR 3–25 cr deposits to fund 18.6% advance growth — and still got cost of deposits down. That is a
  liability-management call, not a franchise failure, but it structurally caps NIM upside.
- **Financialization of household savings is now stated by a PSU bank as its own deposit headwind** — "there has
  been a structural change as far as the saving pattern is concerned in India… investing also in equity, in mutual
  fund, in insurance products and also… gold and… real estate." The CASA-erosion trade and the AMC/broking
  bull-case are the same trade seen from opposite sides of the balance sheet.
- **The FCNR window is being used as a NIM instrument, not a deposit-mobilisation exercise** — CRR/SLR-exempt,
  RBI-hedged, ~50 bps clean spread vs ~7% bulk deposits. The USD 1.2 bn is small versus a INR 9.58 lakh cr deposit
  base, but it lands entirely on the marginal cost of funds, which is what the 2.55–2.60% NIM guide depends on.
- **The gold-loan book is the quietest big number on the call** — INR 57,000 cr growing 52% YoY at 9.10% yield with
  <INR 100 cr NPA. It was not in the opening remarks and only surfaced because an analyst noticed it was missing
  from slide 7 ("somehow gold loans is not mentioned here").
- **The international strategy has inverted:** BOI is now *shrinking* its highest-volume international product (32%
  trade finance) to lift margin — expect flattering NIM and unflattering international growth in the same prints.
- **ECLGS uptake is a leading stress indicator, not a positive.** INR 6,000 cr sanctioned rising to a projected
  INR 8,000 cr means MSME working-capital cycles are stretching; the SMA book looks clean *partly because* the
  scheme is absorbing it.
- **No AS-15 reversal while peers took one** means BOI's Q1 PAT is cleaner than a like-for-like peer comparison
  suggests — a rare case where the conservative bank prints the bigger growth number anyway.

other.body:
- [Asset quality] "Asset quality strengthened in Q1 FY27: Driven by lower Gross NPA, Net NPA alongside improved Provision Coverage" — Gross NPA ₹14,454 Cr / 1.81% (from ₹19,640 Cr / 2.92% a year earlier), Net NPA ₹4,019 Cr / 0.51% (from ₹4,950 Cr / 0.75%), Provision Coverage 93.83% (from 92.94%), Slippage Ratio 0.24% and Credit Cost 0.15%.
- [Stress pipeline] "Overall SMA reduced by ₹2,924 Cr during Q1 FY27 on YoY basis, with the SMA ratio declining from 1.08% to 0.52%, indicating an improvement in the portfolio" — SMA (₹5 Cr & above) total ₹4,097 Cr at 30.06.26, of which SMA-0 ₹675 Cr, SMA-1 ₹2,844 Cr and SMA-2 ₹578 Cr; corporate SMA-1 alone is ₹2,579 Cr, the single largest bucket.
- [NPA concentration] Gross NPA is overwhelmingly a RAM problem, not a corporate one: at Q1 FY27 Agriculture accounts for ₹6,417 Cr (45% of total), MSME ₹5,488 Cr (38%), Retail ₹1,507 Cr (10%) and Corporate only ₹885 Cr (6%); fresh slippages in Q1 FY27 were Agriculture ₹891 Cr (49%), MSME ₹566 Cr (31%), Retail ₹320 Cr (17%) and Corporate ₹54 Cr (3%).
- [Legacy resolution] "The bank maintains strong provisioning against NCLT accounts, with 94% coverage as on 30.06.26" — 315 accounts, total book outstanding (FB) ₹31,729 Cr, provision held ₹29,872 Cr, with RBI List-1 and List-2 cases 100% provided; separately, "The restructured portfolio is only 0.47% of Gross Advances."
- [Sector exposure] Direct exposure to the Real Estate Sector ₹1,02,938 Cr at 30.06.26 (Residential Mortgage ₹98,395 Cr, CRE ₹4,543 Cr) and NBFC (incl. HFCs) ₹80,900 Cr are the two largest industry exposures; Infrastructure is ₹54,967 Cr, within which Power is ₹35,758 Cr and direct SEB exposure has fallen to ₹9,366 Cr from ₹11,832 Cr a year earlier.
- [Cyber/AI governance] Cyber Security Center of Excellence compliant to RBI CSF 2016 and IT GRC 2024, with ISO 27001:2022, ISO 22301:2019 and PCI DSS certification; the bank has initiated an in-house Digital Forensic Incident Response Lab, AI-enabled red teaming, preparation of a "Quantum safe policy and framework", gap assessment for AI-generated cyber attacks, and "Identification and inventorization of LLMs hosted in Bank"; MuleHunter.AI is deployed for mule-account detection.
- [Overseas group] All five overseas subsidiaries/associates — Bank of India (New Zealand), (Tanzania), (Uganda), PT Bank of India Indonesia Tbk and Indo Zambia Bank — reported profits in Q1 FY 27; overseas advances are split Local Lending 38% / India-Linked 34% / Trade Finance 28%.
- [Ratings] Domestic long-term ratings: CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings and CARE at AA+ (Stable); ACUITE and Informerics at AAA (Stable). Domestic short term: CRISIL A1+ and CARE A1+. Overseas: Fitch Ratings BBB-(Long)/F3(Short) (Stable).
